 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 13, 2026, 11:47:09 AM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 8th Pay Commission calculator: The growth of central government employees' salaries heavily relies on fitment factors and annual increment rates. Various organizations have proposed differing fitment factors and increment rates for the 8th Pay Commission. Salary estimates reveal the potential financial impacts for Level 5-7 employees based on varying conditions. A high increment rate could potentially close the salary gap over time compared to a high fitment factor. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online 8th Pay Commission salary calculator for Level 5-7 employees The growth in the basic salary of central government employees is determined by two key factors: the fitment factor and the annual increment rate. A high increment rate can considerably increase your basic pay at the time of pay revision, while a high fitment factor can accelerate your salary growth over the years. But what can happen if the 8th Pay Commission delivers a low fitment factor and increases the annual increment rate?
To see the difference, let’s first look at the fitment factor and the increment rate under the 7th Pay Commission and compare them with a scenario involving high increment rate and a high fitment factor.
Under the 7th Pay Commission, the fitment factor is 2.57, and the annual increment rate is 3%. For the 8th Pay Commission, central government employee associations have been demanding a fitment factor of up to 4.38. They are also demanding an increase in the annual increment to 7%. 
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission news: Notified a year ago, 5 biggest 8th CPC developments since November 3, 2025 
 Fitment factor recommendations for 8 th Pay Commission 
Most employees and pensioners organisations, including the National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM), have recommended a 3.833 fitment factor for employees. If accepted, this would raise the minimum salary from Rs 18,000 under the 7th Pay Commission to Rs 69,000 under the 8th Pay Commission.
However, many experts say the 8th CPC may decide on a fitment factor of up to 2.5. However, it will be known only when the government notifies the 8th Pay Commission report.

 Increment rate recommendations for 8 th Pay Commission 
Recommendations to the 8th Pay Commission about the fitment factor also vary. Several bodies, including the NC-JCM, the All India Defence Employees’ Federation (AIDEF), the Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO), are demanding a 6% annual increment. However, some organisations, such as the All India New Pension Scheme Employees Federation (AINPSEF), have recommended a 7% increment rate.

 High fitment factor vs high increment rate: Salary estimates for Level 5-7 employees 
The basic argument behind recommending a high increment rate is that it will reduce the dependency on the 10-yearly basic salary revision through a pay commission. The AINPSEF says that with a 7% increment rate, the gross salary of a central government employee will double in 7-8 years.
Also Read: 8th Pay Commission: 6 key demands by Railway employee's body; better pay, merging of pay scales, hardship allowance and more 
Here, through estimates, we will show the difference in salaries of Level 5-7 employees’ basic pay in 1, 5 and 10 years at different increment rates and fitment factors. For calculations, we are assuming three conditions.
 2.57 fitment factor, 3% increment rate
 2.1 fitment factor, 7% increment rate
 2.57 fitment factor, 7% increment rate
 Level 5 salary estimates under high increment rate vs high fitment factor 
Level 5 basic pay as per the 7th Pay Commission = Rs 29,200
 Path Year 1 basic Year 5 basic Year 10 basic 
 2.57 fitment factor, 3%/yr increment ₹ 75,044 ₹ 84,463 ₹ 97,915 
 2.1 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 61,320 ₹ 80,378 ₹ 1,12,734 
 2.57 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 75,044 ₹ 98,367 ₹ 1,37,965 
 Level 6 salary estimates under high increment rate vs high fitment factor 
Level 6 basic pay as per the 7th Pay Commission= Rs 35,400
 Path Year 1 basic Year 5 basic Year 10 basic 
 2.57 fitment factor, 3%/yr increment ₹ 90,978 ₹ 1,02,397 ₹ 1,18,706 
 2.1 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 74,340 ₹ 97,445 ₹ 1,36,671 
 2.57 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 90,978 ₹ 1,19,254 ₹ 1,67,259 
 Level 7 salary estimates under high increment rate vs high fitment factor 
Level 7 basic pay as per the 7th Pay Commission= Rs 44,900
 Path Year 1 basic Year 5 basic Year 10 basic 
 2.57 fitment factor, 3%/yr increment ₹ 1,15,393 ₹ 1,29,876 ₹ 1,50,562 
 2.1 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 94,290 ₹ 1,23,595 ₹ 1,73,348 
 2.57 fitment factor, 7%/yr increment ₹ 1,15,393 ₹ 1,51,257 ₹ 2,12,145 
 From the above estimates, you can see that with a high increment rate, salary growth may not be as significant as it would be with a high fitment factor and a 3% growth rate. But the gap narrows in 5 years, while in 10 years, a high annual increment rate leaves the payout of a high fitment factor far behind.
But how a high increment rate or the fitment factor impacts the payouts of employees will be known when the 8th Pay Commission report is implemented. ( Originally published on Nov 12, 2026 ) (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
